prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A dual-aperture zoom digital camera operable in both still and video modes. The camera includes Wide and Tele imaging sections with respective lens/sensor combinations and image signal processors and a camera controller operatively coupled to the Wide and Tele imaging sections. The Wide and Tele imaging sections provide respective image data. The controller is configured to combine in still mode at least some of the Wide and Tele image data to provide a fused output image from a particular point of view, and to provide without fusion continuous zoom video mode output images, each output image having a given output resolution, wherein the video mode output images are provided with a smooth transition when switching between a lower zoom factor (ZF) value and a higher ZF value or vice versa, and wherein at the lower ZF the output resolution is determined by the Wide sensor while at the higher ZF value the output resolution is determined by the Tele sensor.

outputs.L3:
The camera is a dual-aperture zoom digital camera configured to operate in both still-image mode and video mode. It includes two separate imaging sections: a Wide imaging section and a Tele imaging section. Each imaging section has its own optical path, including a dedicated lens, an image sensor, and an image signal processor. The Wide imaging section is configured to capture image data over a wider field of view, while the Tele imaging section is configured to capture image data at a narrower field of view and higher magnification.

A camera controller is coupled to both imaging sections and receives image data from the Wide and Tele image signal processors. The controller manages operation of the camera, including selection, processing, and coordination of image data received from the two imaging sections.

When operating in still mode, the camera controller combines at least some of the image data captured by the Wide imaging section with at least some of the image data captured by the Tele imaging section. This combination produces a fused output image corresponding to a particular point of view. The fused image may use information from both imaging sections to provide improved image quality, detail, or zoom performance.

When operating in video mode, the camera provides a continuous zoom output without fusing the Wide and Tele image data. Instead, the camera transitions smoothly between lower zoom factors and higher zoom factors by selecting or switching between image data from the Wide and Tele imaging sections as needed. This enables continuous zoom video capture while avoiding fusion artifacts and maintaining smooth visual transitions across the zoom range.
outputs.L4:
A dual-aperture zoom digital camera includes two separate imaging sections: a Wide imaging section and a Tele imaging section. Each imaging section includes its own optical lens assembly, image sensor, and image-processing path, allowing the camera to capture image data simultaneously or selectively from two different fields of view. The Wide imaging section is configured to capture a relatively wide field of view and is used for lower zoom factors, while the Tele imaging section is configured to capture a narrower field of view and is used for higher zoom factors. A camera controller coordinates the operation of the two imaging sections, receives image data from the dedicated processors, and determines how the captured data should be used for still-image capture and video capture.

In still-image mode, the controller may combine, align, or fuse image data obtained from the Wide and Tele imaging sections to generate a final output image. The fusion process can use information from both apertures to improve image quality, preserve detail, reduce noise, enhance resolution, or provide a selected viewpoint. Depending on the selected zoom factor and scene conditions, the camera may choose one imaging section as the primary viewpoint and supplement it with data from the other imaging section. The resulting still image may therefore benefit from the Wide camera’s broader scene coverage and the Tele camera’s higher-resolution detail in a narrower field of view.

In video mode, the controller manages zoom operation so that the user experiences a smooth and continuous zoom transition. At lower zoom settings, the output video is determined primarily from the Wide imaging section. At higher zoom settings, the output video is determined primarily from the Tele imaging section. Between these ranges, the controller blends, switches, crops, scales, or otherwise processes image data from the two imaging sections to avoid abrupt jumps in magnification, field of view, exposure, color, or perspective. This allows the video stream to transition continuously from a Wide-based zoom region to a Tele-based zoom region while maintaining stable image quality and a natural visual appearance.

The system may also compensate for differences between the two imaging sections, such as different optical axes, focal lengths, sensor resolutions, color responses, lens distortions, exposure settings, or focus positions. Calibration and image-registration data may be used to align the Wide and Tele images before fusion or transition processing. The controller may further adjust white balance, brightness, contrast, sharpness, and geometric mapping so that images from the two apertures match closely when combined or when switching dominance during zoom.

By using two dedicated apertures rather than relying solely on digital cropping from a single sensor, the camera can provide improved zoom performance in a compact device. The Wide imaging section supports broad scene capture and lower zoom levels, while the Tele imaging section provides additional detail at higher zoom levels. Together, the two imaging paths enable high-quality fused still images and smooth continuous video zoom across a zoom range that would otherwise be difficult to achieve with a single-aperture digital camera.

**The Wide Tele**

The wide tele lens offers a unique way to capture the world. It combines a broader view with the power to bring distant subjects closer, making it useful for landscapes, travel photography, events, and creative storytelling. With this type of lens, photographers can show more of the scene while still keeping attention on important details.

The wide tele perspective is especially helpful when you want depth and atmosphere in an image. It can make mountains look dramatic, streets feel alive, and portraits appear natural within their surroundings. Instead of isolating a subject completely, it allows the background to remain part of the story.

Whether used by beginners or professionals, the wide tele approach encourages creativity. It helps photographers explore space, distance, and composition in new ways. The result is often a balanced image that feels both expansive and focused.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical description of a smartphone camera system with Wide and Tele imaging sections, each having its own ISP, controlled to provide fused still images and smooth continuous zoom video output.
counterfactuals.output:
A smartphone camera system includes a multi-aperture imaging architecture having at least a Wide imaging section and a Tele imaging section. The Wide imaging section includes a Wide lens assembly, a Wide image sensor, and a dedicated Wide image signal processor (Wide ISP). The Tele imaging section includes a Tele lens assembly, a Tele image sensor, and a dedicated Tele image signal processor (Tele ISP). The Wide and Tele imaging sections are optically and electronically arranged to capture at least partially overlapping fields of view, enabling image fusion and continuous zoom operation across a range of effective focal lengths.

The Wide ISP is coupled to the Wide image sensor and is configured to receive raw Wide image data, perform sensor correction, demosaicing, noise reduction, tone mapping, color correction, sharpening, lens shading correction, geometric distortion correction, and exposure-related processing. The Tele ISP is coupled to the Tele image sensor and is configured to independently process raw Tele image data using corresponding image-processing operations optimized for the Tele optical path and sensor characteristics. Each ISP may further generate metadata including exposure time, analog and digital gain, white-balance gains, lens position, focus distance, optical image stabilization state, rolling-shutter timing, depth or confidence information, and image-quality metrics.

A camera controller coordinates operation of the Wide and Tele imaging sections. The controller synchronizes image capture timing between the Wide and Tele sensors, controls exposure and gain for each sensor, manages autofocus and optical stabilization, and configures the Wide ISP and Tele ISP according to the selected capture mode. The controller may include or communicate with a fusion processor, application processor, graphics processor, neural processing unit, or other computational imaging engine.

For still image capture, the system may operate the Wide and Tele imaging sections concurrently. The Wide ISP produces a processed Wide image stream or frame, and the Tele ISP produces a processed Tele image stream or frame. The camera controller aligns the Wide and Tele images using calibration data that includes relative focal length, principal point, lens distortion, sensor alignment, baseline, field-of-view overlap, and parallax parameters. The aligned image data is fused to generate a composite still image. In one implementation, the Wide image contributes scene context, lower-noise image regions, and wide field-of-view content, while the Tele image contributes higher spatial-frequency detail in overlapping regions. The fusion process may include spatial registration, exposure matching, color matching, local motion detection, occlusion handling, parallax compensation, multi-scale blending, super-resolution, denoising, and artifact suppression. The resulting still image may have an effective field of view corresponding to a user-selected zoom level while maintaining improved resolution, noise performance, and dynamic range compared with a single-camera capture.

For video capture, the camera controller provides a smooth continuous zoom output by selectively combining and transitioning between the Wide and Tele image streams. At lower zoom ratios, the output video may be generated primarily from the Wide imaging section using digital crop and scaling. At higher zoom ratios, the output video may be generated primarily from the Tele imaging section. In an intermediate zoom range, the controller blends or fuses the Wide and Tele streams to provide a continuous change in effective focal length without an abrupt visual switch. The system may adjust crop windows, scaling factors, stabilization margins, tone mapping, color response, noise reduction strength, and sharpening parameters over time so that the video output exhibits consistent brightness, color, perspective, focus, and motion characteristics during zooming.

The Wide ISP and Tele ISP may operate simultaneously during continuous zoom video. Each ISP processes its respective sensor stream at the video frame rate and provides processed frames and metadata to a zoom compositor. The zoom compositor performs frame synchronization, geometric warping, electronic image stabilization, rolling-shutter compensation, field-of-view matching, exposure and white-balance matching, temporal filtering, and blending. The compositor may dynamically weight the Wide and Tele streams as a function of zoom factor, scene content, light level, motion, focus confidence, and occlusion confidence. For example, as the zoom factor increases, the output may transition from a Wide-derived image to a fused Wide/Tele image and then to a Tele-derived image. The transition may be temporally smoothed to avoid jumps in framing, color, noise, sharpness, or perspective.

The system may maintain separate exposure and focus control loops for the Wide and Tele imaging sections while applying coordinated constraints to reduce visible differences between streams. In bright conditions, both imaging sections may be operated with synchronized exposures to facilitate fusion. In low-light conditions, the controller may favor the Wide imaging section for lower noise while using Tele data selectively for detail enhancement when sufficient signal quality exists. If the Tele image is unavailable, out of focus, occluded, or misaligned due to close subject parallax, the controller may reduce the Tele contribution and generate the output from the Wide image stream.

Calibration data stored in non-volatile memory may be used by the ISPs and camera controller to correct optical and sensor variations. The calibration data may include intrinsic parameters for each camera, extrinsic parameters between cameras, lens distortion models, shading maps, color correction matrices, modulation transfer function data, focus-dependent alignment tables, optical image stabilization transfer functions, and temperature-dependent correction factors. The calibration data enables accurate registration and consistent rendering between the Wide and Tele sections.

The architecture allows the Wide and Tele imaging sections to operate as independent imaging pipelines while being coordinated at a system level. Dedicated ISPs reduce processing latency and allow each sensor-lens combination to be optimized independently. The fused still-image mode provides enhanced image quality by combining complementary information from the Wide and Tele cameras, and the continuous zoom video mode provides a visually smooth zoom experience by transitioning between and blending the independently processed image streams.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
